question: Why is current Fovelle empty-window launch-to-menus readiness slower than qView 7.1?
baseline_definition: Process spawn through both first event loop and menu readiness. Not optical first frame or just first event loop.
method: Same Qt 6.11.2 arm64 -O3 Release build, maximized empty windows, fresh isolated INI, no images; warm up once then 20 alternating measured samples per executable per experiment. Parent monotonic timestamp; normal process exits.
primary_finding: Deferred menu materialization after two queued zero-timer turns is the dominant location of the observed extra time. A menus-before-show intervention with identical menu work materially reduces total startup time.

key_mapping.qview: Fovelle-menu-profile, same deferred behavior as production
key_mapping.fovelle: Fovelle-eager-menu, experimental ensureMenus called at end of constructor before native show

intervention.changes: Only timing instrumentation and insertion of if (deferMenus) ensureMenus() at constructor end. Identical menu creation and state synchronization are retained. No production source changes.

hypotheses.evidence: Fovelle mean 93.79 ms, qView mean 103.96 ms in common-stages.
Measured state synchronization mean around 0.054 ms.
Settings preparation Fovelle mean 4.85 ms versus qView 0.89 ms.

hypotheses.status: Not supported by the boundary measurements
hypotheses.evidence: Spawn to identity gap mean approximately 3.28 ms. This is a broad boundary, not a direct dyld attribution.

hypotheses.hypothesis: RAW/HDR decoding or background network updates dominate
hypotheses.evidence: No image input, HDRRenderer created on postLoad; update feed/key empty, initializer returns before Sparkle updater controller starts.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Default maximization is the sole cause
hypotheses.status: Contradicted by previous matched-maximized and current profiles
hypotheses.evidence: Both processes request Maximized before show in these tests.

limits: Do not add medians to explain a total; common-stage contributions use means.
A zero timer is not an explicit fixed sleep. Its ordering relative to other event sources is unspecified. The pre-menu gap includes dispatch and intervening events, not necessarily pure idle time.
The tree builder was measured as a unit; individual AppKit calls inside it have not been assigned exact shares.
The experiment supports a causal timing effect, not a claim that every residual millisecond or all feature workloads are explained.
Experimental variant has not undergone the full production acceptance suite and is not a shipped fix.
Boundary receipt times include small logging/parent scheduling overhead; results vary by batch and should not be substituted for the previous comparison medians.
